source: Two charts read on 12 Oct 2026: startup drawdowns from 2021–22 peak marks, and a modeled mid/senior grant from late 2022 to Oct 2026. Headline valuations, not per-share. Common often got less. Gopuff's latest mark is a 2022 secondary.

notes: Historical multiples are worth-now divided by the grant at entry. The source chart already nets out dilution, is pre-tax, and includes no refreshers.

The forward slider splits that into two pieces: how many times the company mark rises, and what fraction of your percent you keep. Net multiple = mark multiple × fraction kept. Set the fraction to 100% if the number in your head is already a chart-style net multiple.
Under $1B the grant is a percent of the company, using the source chart's bands. At $1B or more the grant is a flat $200k, so the percent shrinks as the price rises.
At $50B or more, if the lab switch is on, the grant becomes $2M over four years. That is OpenAI's 2023 level from the chart ($500k a year), not a 2026 offer letter.
The public preset uses Nvidia's 2022 package from the same chart: $80k a year, times four. It is not a quote for joining Nvidia now.
Reported private marks used as presets: Anthropic about $965B after the May 2026 round, OpenAI about $852B after the spring 2026 round. Higher numbers were being discussed and were not closed.

Where a 2022 grant fits two ownership bands, the map states the band it used. Cursor, ElevenLabs, and Harvey use 0.20% because the grant is what that band produces and the companies were founded in 2022. Grants from $200k to $500k use 0.10%. A flat $200k is treated as the $1B+ cap, not as a precise valuation.

Four companies the chart only calls unicorns are plotted at $1B. Northvolt is plotted on the $14B+ it raised, because the chart gives capital raised rather than a valuation. Cameo's latest point is 10% of $1B, from a 90% down round. Bright Health, Truepill, and Chime stay in the table: the chart doesn't give a company valuation for them.
Sierra was founded in 2023. That row, and OpenEvidence, are the chart's stage-sized grant, not proof someone started in October 2022.

winners.name: Cursor
winners.why: The editor was where the work already happened, and cheaper inference widened the margin on a product people were paying for. The grant matches 0.20% of about $56M; the other reading, 0.10%, would be $113M. Anysphere was founded in 2022.

winners.name: Anthropic
winners.why: Levels.fyi on the chart is about $200k a year of equity, times four. The company was already a lab, and the share price still had a long way to rerate. 95x is net of dilution.

winners.name: OpenAI
winners.why: The chart's OpenAI package is about $500k a year in 2023, times four. Same era as Anthropic, smaller multiple, because the grant was already $2M. The January 2023 Microsoft round was around $29B.

winners.name: Cognition
winners.why: Coding agents. A $350k grant is 0.10% of $350M under the chart's rule. The category was not priced as infrastructure yet.

winners.name: Figure
winners.why: Humanoid robots. Atoms paid here because the pitch was labor with a buyer, not a factory hoping for the next round. $400k is 0.10% of $400M.

winners.name: Perplexity
winners.why: An answer product people used. $184k fits either 0.20% of $92M or 0.10% of $184M. Both are still a startup entry.

winners.name: ElevenLabs
winners.why: Voice as a pipeline, not a demo. $18k is 0.20% of about $9M. The multiple is the entry price.

winners.name: Harvey
winners.why: Legal work already had a budget and a matter file. $60k is 0.20% of about $30M.

winners.name: Helsing
winners.why: European defense software. The grant was large because the company was already raising. 27x is the modest end of this chart. $454k is 0.10% of $454M.

winners.name: Mistral
winners.why: A lab still priced like a growth company. $260k is 0.10% of $260M.

winners.name: Polymarket
winners.why: A venue. The right to operate and the volume showed up after the grant. The chart's $10M and 30x don't multiply back exactly; both numbers are theirs.

winners.name: Mercer
winners.why: The chart groups Mercer with AI apps: $250k to $9.2M, 37x. There isn't a cleaner public description on the chart, so this map doesn't invent a product story.

winners.name: Baseten
winners.why: Inference infrastructure. $200k is the chart's flat package once a private company is worth $1B or more, so this dot is not a precise entry valuation.

winners.name: Saronic
winners.why: Autonomous boats, sold into defense. $174k fits 0.20% of $87M or 0.10% of $174M.

winners.name: Nvidia
winners.why: Public RSUs. The chart's Levels.fyi note is about $80k a year, times four. 19x, against about 2.2x for a typical S&P grant over the same window. You could sell along the way. Refreshers are not in the number.

winners.name: CoreWeave
winners.why: GPU cloud, the chart's public color. $200k grant, 20x. It rented out the scarce input.

winners.name: Legora
winners.why: Legal software, a smaller multiple than Harvey. $180k fits 0.20% of $90M or 0.10% of $180M.

winners.name: Replit
winners.why: A developer product people already knew. $400k is 0.10% of $400M. Early on a calendar, late on a price.

winners.name: Sierra
winners.why: Customer-facing agents. Sierra was founded in 2023, so this is the chart's stage-sized $200k grant, not a late-2022 start date.

winners.name: Palantir
winners.why: Public. About $40k a year on the chart, times four. 17x. The government workflow was already the system of record.

winners.name: OpenEvidence
winners.why: Clinical answers. A stage-sized $200k grant and 13x. Treat the start date as the chart's model.

winners.name: Groq
winners.why: Inference chips. The $200k flat grant means the chart already treated the company as a $1B+ private. 12x from there.

winners.name: SpaceX
winners.why: A late-stage private grant of $200k, 10x by Oct 2026. The chart groups it with public stock, which is a statement about 2026, not about 2022.

winners.name: Runway
winners.why: Video generation. $250k is 0.10% of $250M, or the edge of the 0.05% band. 8x.

winners.name: Kalshi
winners.why: Regulated event contracts. A $200k flat grant and 9x. Relative to Polymarket, more of the outcome was already in the entry price.

peaks.name: FTX
peaks.why: Fraud. There was no business behind the mark.

peaks.name: Byju's
peaks.why: Education growth bought with capital, then a governance failure. Equity to zero.

peaks.name: Northvolt
peaks.why: Battery factories. The chart says $14B+ raised and $0 of equity. Plotted on capital raised.

peaks.name: Olive AI
peaks.why: Hospital software sold as AI. It stayed a services business and shut down.

peaks.name: Convoy
peaks.why: Freight brokerage. The take rate did not survive a normal freight market.

peaks.name: Builder.ai
peaks.why: Software margins claimed on human labor. Insolvent.

peaks.name: Bird
peaks.why: Scooters. Depreciation, city rules, and a subsidy. The chart says unicorn to bankrupt, so this dot is placed at $1B.

peaks.name: Bowery Farming
peaks.why: Indoor farming. Power and capex against the price of a crop. Placed at $1B because the chart only says unicorn.

peaks.name: Veev
peaks.why: Prefab construction. Project capex. Placed at $1B because the chart only says unicorn.

peaks.name: Zeus Living
peaks.why: Corporate housing after a travel boom. Wound down. Placed at $1B because the chart only says unicorn.

peaks.name: Hopin
peaks.why: Virtual events after lockdowns. $7.75B to a $15M sale of the core.

peaks.name: Bright Health
peaks.why: Health insurance. Down 99% from the 2021 IPO. The chart gives no peak valuation, so it stays off the scatter.

peaks.name: Miro
peaks.why: Collaboration software people still use. $17.5B to $1.36B. The product survived the price.

peaks.name: Cameo
peaks.why: Celebrity shout-outs. The chart says a round at 90% off the $1B mark, so the latest dot is placed at $100M.

peaks.name: Klarna
peaks.why: Buy-now-pay-later. $45.6B to about $6.7B. Still operating. The loss belongs to the 2021 entry.

peaks.name: Airtable
peaks.why: Horizontal software. $11.7B to $2.25B. Seats slowed; the company did not vanish.

peaks.name: Getir
peaks.why: Quick commerce. $11.8B to $2.5B. Delivery cost was the product.

peaks.name: Instacart
peaks.why: Grocery delivery. $39B to about $9.6B. A real business that was marked for a monopoly it did not have.

peaks.name: Checkout.com
peaks.why: Payments. $40B to $12B. Someone hired at $12B is not holding the peak grant.

peaks.name: Truepill
peaks.why: Digital pharmacy, about two-thirds below the 2021 peak. No dollar pair on the chart.

peaks.name: Brex
peaks.why: Corporate cards. $12.3B to $4.5B.

peaks.name: Chime
peaks.why: Neobank. The chart gives a share price, $69 to about $33, not a company valuation. 33/69 is about 48%.

peaks.name: Gopuff
peaks.why: Delivery. $17B to $8.3B, and the chart dates that latest figure to a 2022 secondary. Stale.

peaks.name: Discord
peaks.why: A product people use. $15B to $8.5B. A grant struck at today's mark is a new bet.

peaks.name: Plaid
peaks.why: Bank connectivity. $13.4B to $8B. The drawdown is the peak entry, not a reason to ignore the company at the new price.
